reason: The elite figure in this passage is Reuel, the priest of Midian, who is portrayed favorably. He demonstrates hospitality and wisdom by welcoming the stranger (Moses) when his daughters report how this man helped them, and he subsequently gives his daughter Zipporah to Moses in marriage. The unfavorable portrayal is applied instead to the shepherds (הרעים), who are common laborers rather than elite, as they drive away the priest's daughters from the well.
